- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +0.33 or higher) and news volume spikes, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a strong downward sentiment shift (e.g., -0.33 or lower), model often undercorrects — adjust downward by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment remains flat or neutral for 3+ days, model overestimates volatility — dampen forecast variance by 10–15%.
- Model consistently overpredicts short-term (1–7 day) price drops after negative sentiment — apply a 3–5% upward bias to counteract lag.
- When sentiment changes direction mid-period (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment shift.
- If news volume is low (0.0) for 5+ days, model tends to drift toward historical mean — apply mean reversion correction with 1–2% decay per day.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — cap forecast at 1.5x the 30-day moving average to prevent runaway peaks.
- Model underestimates true price range during high sentiment volatility — widen forecast band by 5–10% to capture range-bound behavior.
